summary: This focused pass corrects an overbroad earlier default claim and follows evidence identity through the browser. The callable assessment API defaults to strict missing-check handling, but the UI initializes allow_missing=True. The analysis cache, optional-summary cache and sign-off invalidation use narrower identities than the complete evidence they represent. These are source-level concerns requiring targeted session tests, not observed live-app failures. The receipt's stored evidence digests remain a real strength and are not alleged to be forged.
limitations: Pinned local checkout, not a verified official final-submission receipt; branch names and later changes are outside this pass.
Static source analysis only. No submission code, tests, installers, workflows, notebook, server, hosted endpoint or model was executed.
No sealed envelopes, answer keys or raw clinical datasets were accessed. Numerical correctness, performance, accessibility and fresh-machine setup remain untested.
Source-derived control-flow consequences are labeled as such. Proposed acceptance checks are not observed test results.
The collected text budget is 160 files, 200 KB/file and 4 MB/entry. Complete_with_exclusions is not an exhaustive audit; exclusions and focused follow-ups are recorded.
No official score, cross-team ranking, clinical validity or regulatory/accessibility certification is asserted.

findings.title: The analysis cache signature omits release-file identity
findings.observation: inputs_sig enumerates card YAML and tower Python paths with modification times, but not release data. analyze is decorated with st.cache_data and receives the release path, card ID, missing-check option, that signature and optional custom-card JSON. Reading release bytes happens inside the cached body. Replacing data at the same path does not change the explicitly supplied data identity.
findings.impact: Under the documented cache contract, unchanged arguments and source can reuse an earlier result even when a release file changed in place. This is conditional on path reuse and a retained cache; immutable per-run release directories avoid that condition. It is not evidence that the frozen baseline changed during judging.
findings.recommendation: Pass a content-bound release manifest or immutable release-version identity into every cached analysis and board call. Show which version the result represents and invalidate all derived views together. A code/card timestamp signature should remain a separate policy-version input.
findings.acceptance_check: On invented data, run a comparison, replace one value at the same release path without changing code/cards, and rerun. The cached result must either refresh to the new input digest or explicitly refuse the changed immutable release. Retain an unchanged-input cache-hit control.
findings.confidence: High for the inspected cache arguments and official cache contract; stale-result behavior has not been reproduced here.

findings.title: The AI citation caption accurately describes an ID-membership check
findings.observation: The checker identifies unknown finding/sample references and whether the verdict word appears. The UI describes its result narrowly as an ID existing in this result, rather than claiming that all prose is factually verified. The system prompt separately tells the model to use only supplied facts and avoid clinical advice.
findings.impact: This appropriately limits what an automated citation check proves. Existing IDs and a verdict word do not validate numbers, negation or the meaning of a generated sentence, so the narrow caption is a strength worth preserving.
findings.recommendation: Keep the scoped label and deterministic verdict as authoritative. Add evidence-version binding and targeted contradictory-number/negation cases before making any broader factual-validation claim.
findings.acceptance_check: With mocked responses, compare an unknown ID, a known ID with an unsupported numeric statement, and the wrong verdict embedded in a negation. Keep identity checks separate from semantic correctness and do not label all passing IDs as verified facts.
findings.confidence: High for checker and caption wording. The test file contains definitions, not this reviewer's observed test results, and no model was called.

evidence.quote:
def check(text: str, ready: dict, findings: dict | None) -> dict:
    """Every finding and sample id the text cites must be one the model was given: a release change that touches
    this question, or a sample named in this question's results."""
    ctx = context(ready, findings)
    known_f = {f["id"] for f in ctx.get("release_changes_that_touch_this_question", [])}
    known_s = set(SAMPLE.findall(json.dumps(ctx, default=str)))
    cited_f = sorted(set(FINDING.findall(text)), key=lambda x: int(x[1:]))
    cited_s = sorted(set(SAMPLE.findall(text)))
    unknown = [x for x in cited_f if x not in known_f] + [
        s for s in cited_s if s not in known_s and not any(k.startswith(s + "-") for k in known_s)]
    states = bool(re.search(rf"\b{re.escape(ready['verdict'])}\b", text, re.I))
    return {"cited": len(cited_f) + len(cited_s), "unknown": unknown, "states_verdict": states}

SYSTEM = """You write a short plain-English summary of a data-quality tool's results for a research data engineer.
Rules:
- Use only facts in the JSON you are given. Never add numbers, sample ids, causes or advice that are not in it.
- Start with the verdict for the research question, using the exact verdict word.
- Then say which release changes touch this question and why they matter. If none touch it, say so and explain the verdict from the reasons.
- Cite only the finding ids listed under release_changes_that_touch_this_question, in square brackets, like [F1]. Never put anything else in square brackets.
- Then give the first next step and one thing the tool can't tell.
- Write 4 to 6 sentences in one paragraph: no lists, no headings, no em dashes.
- No diagnosis, treatment advice or clinical claims."""

def test_a_change_that_does_not_touch_the_question_counts_as_unknown(self):
        c = ai.check("Conditional, because of [F2] and TCGA-E2-A1L7-01.", READY, FINDINGS)
        self.assertEqual(c["unknown"], ["F2", "TCGA-E2-A1L7-01"])

    def test_citations_flag_ids_that_are_not_in_the_results(self):
        c = ai.check("Conditional: [F1] swapped TCGA-A8-A09K-01 with TCGA-ZZ-0000-01, see [F7].", READY, FINDINGS)
        self.assertEqual(c["unknown"], ["F7", "TCGA-ZZ-0000-01"])
        self.assertEqual(c["cited"], 4)
        self.assertTrue(c["states_verdict"])

    def test_a_patient_level_id_counts_as_found(self):
        self.assertEqual(ai.check("TCGA-A8-A09K was swapped.", READY, FINDINGS)["unknown"], [])

    def test_summary_strips_thinking_and_checks_it(self):
        with mock.patch.object(ai, "ask", return_value=("<think>notes</think>Conditional. [F1] matters.", "fake")):
            out = ai.summarize(READY, FINDINGS)
        self.assertEqual(out["text"], "Conditional. [F1] matters.")
        self.assertEqual(out["citations"], {"cited": 1, "unknown": []})
        self.assertTrue(out["states_verdict"])

findings.title: The browser enables permissive missing-check handling by default
findings.observation: The sidebar sets st.session_state.allow_missing to True when the key is absent and passes that value into analyze and assess. With this option, an unregistered required check is unknown but nonmaterial. The callable assess and run_checks signatures default to False. Thus the strict API default and permissive browser default are different source facts.
findings.impact: If a required check is unavailable, a fresh browser session can exclude it from the deciding material set unless the user changes Settings. The UI does disclose pending checks and its toggle meaning; this is an active default-policy concern, not a hidden setting or proof that every current card is incomplete.
findings.recommendation: Make strict handling the initial browser default, or give permissive runs a distinct incomplete/development state that cannot be confused with ordinary readiness. Keep the disclosure and test the browser entry point separately from the core API.
findings.acceptance_check: In an authorized fresh-session test with a synthetic card requiring an unregistered check, inspect the initial toggle and resulting state. Compare the strict API, initial UI and explicit permissive opt-in. No ordinary approved result should conceal the pending requirement.
findings.confidence: High for initialization and call flow. The browser was not executed by this reviewer; an API-only default probe does not answer this UI question.

def run_checks(release, card: dict, allow_missing: bool = False) -> list[Issue]:
    """Run every check the card lists.

    A listed check that doesn't exist yet comes back as 'unknown' (material), which makes the verdict Insufficient
    Evidence: the honest answer when part of the question can't be judged. While checks are still being written,
    allow_missing=True lists them as pending without letting them decide the verdict.
    """
    load_all()
    out: list[Issue] = []
    for name in card.get("checks", []):
        fn = CHECKS.get(name)
        if fn is None:
            broken = "; ".join(f"{k}.py: {v}" for k, v in LOAD_ERRORS.items())
            out.append(Issue(id=name, title=f"Check '{name}' is not built yet"
                             + (f" (or its file failed to load: {broken})" if broken else ""), status="unknown",
                             material=not allow_missing, pre_existing=False, numbers={"pending": True},
                             limitation="The tool cannot judge this part of the question yet."))
            continue
        try:
            got = fn(release, card)
            if not isinstance(got, list) or not all(isinstance(x, Issue) for x in got):
                raise TypeError("it must return a list of Issue objects")
            out.extend(got)
        except Exception as e:      # a broken check must never take the whole report down
            out.append(Issue(id=name, title=f"Check '{name}' failed: {e}", status="unknown", material=True,
                             pre_existing=False, limitation="The check crashed, so this part can't be judged."))
    return out

findings.title: Sign-off invalidation does not compare the evidence digests
findings.observation: signed stores findings and readiness digests in the receipt. The live UI's separate signature contains current repair/issue decisions, verdict, sign-off choice, note and reviewer fields, but no findings/readiness digest, input-file digest or complete card policy. It clears signed state only when that narrower signature changes, and the overview reports Signed whenever the retained signed object exists.
findings.impact: A changed policy or refreshed evidence can retain the same verdict and decision IDs while differing from the evidence a reviewer signed. The saved old receipt still identifies its old evidence; the concern is associating that retained sign-off state with a newly displayed result. This narrows the earlier broad claim that any input change withdraws sign-off.
findings.recommendation: Build the live invalidation identity from the same canonical evidence/policy digests used in the receipt, alongside reviewer decisions. Preserve the old receipt as history and require a new decision for a changed evidence version. Exclude only documented nondeterministic display fields from canonicalization.
findings.acceptance_check: Sign an invented result, then change a card's material policy or evidence while keeping verdict and decision IDs the same. After recomputation, the current result must be Pending or explicitly show that the retained signature covers an older version. The original receipt must remain unchanged.
findings.confidence: High for the missing fields in the invalidation signature and the Signed display predicate; no session-level reproduction was executed here.

findings.title: The optional summary cache is keyed only by release label and card ID
findings.observation: ai_box retrieves generated text under ai|release_label|card_id and reuses it until the user requests another summary. That key excludes current findings, readiness, card policy and missing-check setting. The analysis path can recompute when those settings or card timestamps change, while the stored summary remains under the same key.
findings.impact: Optional prose can describe an older result beside a newly recomputed verdict or reason. The UI's accurate citation-ID captions do not establish that cached prose belongs to the current evidence version. No stale model output or provider call was observed in this review.
findings.recommendation: Bind the summary to a canonical digest of the exact context sent to the model. Invalidate or visibly mark old prose when context changes, retain its prior version if useful, and keep deterministic results available without a model.
findings.acceptance_check: Mock model output for one invented context, then change the missing-check policy or a card's reasons with the same release label and card ID. The old summary must disappear or carry an explicit old-version label until regenerated. No network call is required.
findings.confidence: High for session key construction and reuse. Actual model behavior and UI refresh were not tested.

def context(ready: dict, findings: dict | None, release: str | None = None) -> dict:
    """The tool's own results for one question, as the screen shows them. No raw data, and only the release
    changes that touch this question."""
    ctx = {"research_question": ready["card"]["title"], "release": release or ready["release"]["name"],
           "verdict": ready["verdict"], "reasons": list(ready["reasons"])[:6],
           "next_steps": [s["step"] for s in ready.get("next_steps") or []][:4],
           "what_the_tool_cant_tell": list(ready.get("cannot_tell") or [])[:3]}
    if findings:
        touching = {t["finding"] for t in ready.get("release_changes") or []}
        rel = [f for f in findings["findings"] if f["id"] in touching]
        ctx["release_changes_that_touch_this_question"] = [
            {"id": f["id"], "kind": PLAIN.get(f["kind"], f["kind"]), "severity": f["severity"],
             "samples": [e["id"] for e in f["evidence"] if e.get("kind") == "sample"][:12],
             "affects": f.get("affects_analyses") or [], "summary": f["summary"]}
            for f in rel[:12]]
        ctx["release_changes_that_do_not_touch_this_question"] = len(findings["findings"]) - len(rel)
    return ctx
